title: Russian missile strike damages Okhmatdyt children's hospital in Kyiv
body:
On 8 July 2024 Russian missiles struck several Ukrainian cities, and one strike damaged the Okhmatdyt National Children's Hospital in Kyiv, Ukraine's largest children's hospital. According to Human Rights Watch, citing Ukrainian authorities, the attacks that day killed at least 42 civilians, including five children, and injured at least 190 people.

Air raid sirens sounded at 9:52 am, and hundreds of children were evacuated. The first strike hit less than an hour later while patients and staff were still inside, including three patients undergoing heart surgery. Intensive care units and oncology and surgical wings were severely damaged, and the toxicology and traumatology departments were completely destroyed. Ten children were injured at the hospital, and a child evacuated from the intensive care unit in critical condition died in another hospital, as reported on 10 July.

Human Rights Watch said that attacks directed at medical facilities are war crimes under international humanitarian law and that the strike should be investigated as a potential war crime. It noted that at least 1,736 medical facilities in Ukraine had been damaged or destroyed since the full-scale invasion began.
